HUM 100N: This course is an introduction to great ideas, themes, creations, and values in the arts and humanities, emphasizing the development of students' basic interpretive and close reading skills as applied to historically significant works in the various disciplines.
HUM 101: This 3-credit General Humanities (GH) course with an International Cultures (IL) designate offers an introduction to transformative texts from around the world.
HUM 102: This 3-credit General Humanities (GH) course with a United States (US) designate offers an introduction to transformative texts from the beginning of modern history to the present that address current issues in the United States.
HUM 150N: This course is an interdisciplinary, cross-cultural, historical, and contemporary examination of myth as it appears in the visual arts, literature, and film.
HUM 200N: The theme of this course, Explorations in the Humanities: The Quest, is a highly flexible one used to investigate a variety of historically significant works in the arts and humanities from different perspectives-moral, social, historical, literary, artistic, and philosophical.
HUM 220N: Explores the history of AI alongside the evolution of technology and computing.
HUM 297: Formal courses given infrequently to explore, in-depth, a comparatively narrow subject which may be topical or of special interest.
HUM 300N: Two to four (usually three) different interpretive approaches to understanding creative and/or scholarly works in the arts and humanities, as exemplified by the study of specific works organized by theme, topic, or time period(s).
HUM 400N: Advanced interdisciplinary study of a particular theme, period, or topic including materials from various arts and humanities disciplines and interdisciplinary works.
HUM 453: Study of art, literature, film, and other creative genres to illustrate the interrelationships between creative expression and cultural practices.
HUM 460: Analysis of a group of related ideas in art, music, literature, and/or philosophy.
HUM 491: Interdisciplinary studies dealing with selected periods of world culture.
HUM 494: Supervised student activities on research projects identified on an individual or small-group basis.
HUM 495: Supervised internship for undergraduate or graduate Humanities majors in state offices, educational institutions, arts agencies, community organizations, or humanities councils.
HUM 496: Creative projects, including research and design, that are supervised on an individual basis and that fall outside the scope of formal courses.
HUM 497: Formal courses given infrequently to explore, in depth, a comparatively narrow subject that may be topical or of special interest.
HUM 499: Courses offered in foreign countries by individual or group instruction.
